question.problem: In what direction does the function $f(x,y)=x\operatorname{tan}⁡y+2{x}^{2}-\operatorname{ln}⁡x$ decrease most rapidly at the point $(1,\frac{\pi }{4})?$
question.worked_solution:
At a given point, a function $f(x,y)$ decreases most rapidly in the direction opposite to that of its gradient.

So, we compute $-∇f(x,y)$ and evaluate it at the point $(1,\frac{\pi }{4}):$

$$
\begin{aligned}-∇f(x,y) & =-\frac{∂}{∂x}(x\operatorname{tan}⁡y+2{x}^{2}-\operatorname{ln}⁡x)\text{ }i-\frac{∂}{∂y}(x\operatorname{tan}⁡y+2{x}^{2}-\operatorname{ln}⁡x)\text{ }j \\  & =-(\operatorname{tan}⁡y+4x-\frac{1}{x})i-x{sec}^{2}⁡y\text{ }j \\ -∇f(1,\frac{\pi }{4}) & =-(\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})+4\cdot 1-\frac{1}{1})i-1\cdot {sec}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})\text{ }j \\  & =-4\,i-2\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the function decreases most rapidly in the direction of $-4\,i-2\,j.$
